page: Amazon Web Services c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 32-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor based on the x86_64 architecture operating at 3.7 GHz, providing 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of DDR5 running at 5 GHz, delivering a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Hardware-accelerated instruction sets include AVX-512 with support for VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results show strong processor capabilities across single-threaded and multi-threaded evaluations. The instance achieved top-quartile results in stress-ng tests, registering a single-core score of 3076.87 and a multi-core score of 98387.28, which aligns with its Geekbench multi-core rating of 20004.0 and PassMark CPU score of 53519.71. Software compilation throughput is notable, with a Clang compilation score of 44344.0 in Geekbench. In memory testing, cached small-block reads registered 4742.52 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads yielded average-tier throughput at 152.63 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads, prompt processing on a 135M parameter model ranked in the top 10 percent at 4597.95 tokens per second.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated 1:1 physical core-to-vCPU allocation prevents resource contention from simultaneous multithreading, benefiting predictable execution. However, the 2.0 GB per core memory ceiling and the complete absence of local NVMe storage restrict suitability for large in-memory caches or I/O-heavy local scratch tasks. The c7a.8xlarge is suitable for compute-heavy workloads including code compilation, distributed continuous integration pipelines, video encoding, static web rendering, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory at a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Network connectivity provides a 12 Gbps baseline, and the instance includes no bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing highlights strong compute performance, achieving top-quartile scores in stress-ng multi-core metrics, PassMark CPU tests, and software compilation via Clang. Its CPU architecture incorporates AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 acceleration, enabling top-tier inference speeds on small language models. With dedicated core execution and DDR5 memory channels, the c7a.8xlarge is suited for continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, ray tracing, web serving, and CPU-bound analytical jobs.
